2026-11-10T15:59:30.4140675Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4141747Z **Tool retry limit:** if a safe-output tool (for example `push_to_pull_request_branch` or `close_pull_request`) fails, try at most 2 materially different recovery approaches. If the tool still fails, call `report_incomplete` with the error and the approaches attempted, then continue with other work. Do NOT debug underlying infrastructure after repeated failures.
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4142872Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4144104Z **Trust successful tool responses.** Safeoutputs records write transactions that are applied after the agent finishes. A successful safe-output tool call means the transaction was accepted for downstream application. Do NOT independently verify the effect via `gh`, `gh api`, or other GitHub read paths from the current sandbox, because those paths will not reflect future safe-output writes.
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4145354Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4146460Z **Do not inspect infrastructure internals.** When a tool or command fails, do not inspect Docker sockets (`/var/run/docker.sock`), mount tables (`/proc/self/mounts`), container networking (`/proc/net`), `/host` paths, git object storage internals, or container-runtime environment internals. These are outside your control; use `report_incomplete` after the retry limit.
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4147602Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4150800Z temporary_id: optional cross-reference field only for tools whose input schema declares it, including create_issue, create_discussion, and create_pull_request. Do not add it to other tools. Canonical form: '#aw_' followed by 3–12 alphanumeric or underscore characters — e.g., '#aw_abc1', '#aw_pr_fix'. Pattern: /^#?aw_[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,12}$/i (the '#' prefix is optional; bare 'aw_abc1' is accepted and normalised to '#aw_abc1' automatically). Use this form in target fields only where their schema explicitly supports temporary IDs (item_number, issue_number, parent, etc.). In body/markdown text, '#aw_abc1' references are replaced with the real issue/PR/discussion number after creation. Omit entirely when not needed.
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4152983Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4156838Z **Payloads**: safeoutputs tools do NOT support `@filename` expansion. For CLI calls, prefer a complete JSON object inline as one single-quoted shell argument. Inside JSON strings, encode newlines as `\n`, double quotes as `\"`, backslashes as `\\`, and apostrophes as `\u0027`; Unicode can remain literal. Stdin is also supported: `safeoutputs <tool_name> .` reads a complete JSON object from stdin — the entire stdin content must itself be valid JSON; never pipe a raw file or raw Markdown into this bare form. To pass one field's raw text verbatim with no JSON escaping, target that single field instead: `cat file.md | safeoutputs <tool_name> --<field> .` substitutes the field's value with the raw stdin text. Never write a bare `.` as a value inside a quoted JSON literal (e.g. `{"body": .}`) — that is not valid JSON. Do not use auxiliary shell commands or temporary files to construct payloads; the `cat file | ... --field .` form above is the one sanctioned exception, for raw-text fields only. When a native safe-output function is explicitly exposed, pass the fields directly.
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4160506Z </safe-outputs>

2026-11-10T15:59:30.4185016Z Check availability with the metadata-only command `safeoutputs --help`, by itself, in the agent's shell; runner setup logs do not establish sandbox availability. 2026-11-10T15:59:30.4187903Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4189345Z Pass the complete JSON object inline as one single-quoted shell argument. Inside JSON strings, encode newlines as `\n`, double quotes as `\"`, backslashes as `\\`, and apostrophes as `\u0027` so they do not end the shell quote. Unicode can remain literal. The binary comes first, so a malformed payload still runs the CLI and reports an error:
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4190487Z ```bash
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4191013Z safeoutputs add_comment '{"item_number":42,"body":"### Result\n\nIt\u0027s ready.\nQuoted text: \"hello\".\nLiteral path: C:\\temp\\file.txt"}'
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4191565Z ```
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4192310Z This preserves multiline content without auxiliary tools, pipelines, temporary files, or shell expansion. Adapt fields to the enabled tool's schema. Raw Markdown and `@filename` references are not JSON payloads.
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4193031Z 
2026-11-10T15:59:30.4195995Z Stdin is also supported: `safeoutputs <tool_name> .` reads a complete JSON object from stdin — the entire stdin content must itself be valid JSON; never pipe a raw file or raw Markdown into this bare form. Never write a bare `.` as a value inside a quoted JSON literal (e.g. `{"body": .}`) — that is not valid JSON. CLI proxying grants the mounted executable, not auxiliary commands, file writes, or shell expansions beyond the `cat file | ... --field .` form above. Stdin support does not grant permission for redirections. Prefer inline JSON; do not use auxiliary shell commands to construct or submit it.
